_comment: The shared layout-marker palette. CyrFlip draws the marker on four surfaces - the mouse I-beam,
the caret overlay, the tray icon (all three from src/CyrFlip/LayoutStyle.cs) and, inside VS Code,
this extension. They used to carry three separate copies of the table, and the extension's copy
knew only EN/RU/UK: ten of the thirteen curated languages rendered grey there while the app drew
SOURCE OF TRUTH is src/CyrFlip/LayoutStyle.cs - the app ships as one exe with nothing to read at
runtime, so its table has to live in code. This file is the machine-readable copy for everything
outside that exe, and LayoutColorsTests fails the build if the two disagree.
It lives under vscode-extension/src/ rather than assets/ because vsce packages only what is inside
the extension root; a file one directory up would simply be missing from the published .vsix.
Two levels and one exit. 'curated' is the colour of a language - what the marker's two letters
name. 'layouts' is the colour of one keyboard layout, keyed by KLID: US and Dvorak both read 'EN',
so the shade is the only thing that separates them (and in the overlay's dot mode it is the whole
marker). Every shade stays inside its language's hue, so the colour still answers 'which language'
first. Anything else - a Polish keyboard, a Japanese IME - is 'other': one neutral colour, because
there is no honest way to hand out distinct recognisable colours for the ~218 layouts Windows
ships. The letters still name the language there (PL, JA, TR).
The app publishes the active KLID to layout-klid.txt beside layout.txt; when that file is absent
(an older CyrFlip), fall back to the language colour in 'curated'.
_markerOpacityComment: How opaque the marker is drawn over the user's text, in and out of the editor. Mirrors LayoutStyle.MarkerOpacity; LayoutColorsTests fails the build if the two disagree.
